game.title: ENSLAVED: Odyssey to the West
game.build_notes: Verified on Windows 10, 2026-09-03. During testing the window was forced to 1280x720 windowed by a d3d9 proxy; this build ships no windowed mode of its own. Everything below was driven externally against the game window - no in-process code was required for any of it.

api_notes: SendInput is the route that works. Use SCANCODES rather than virtual keys: it keeps keyboard layout out of the path, which is the trap that cost a sibling project (doom-2016-vr) a session.

ARROW KEYS REQUIRE KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY. Without it, scancode 0x50 is numpad-2, the menu ignores it, and nothing errors - it simply reads as 'this game ignores the keyboard'. Observed directly: three Down presses moved the menu selection not at all; with the flag it moved on the first try.
Foreground the window before sending anything, and re-check it. Synthetic input follows focus.
PostMessage(WM_KEYDOWN) was attempted but never soundly measured. Treat as UNKNOWN, not as a negative.

bindings.notes: Held 2.2s; the character visibly advanced. Confirmed by comparing two screenshots, not by a pixel statistic.
SendInput MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE. About 120 steps of dx=40 swung the view through a large arc onto entirely different scenery.

bindings.action: pause / open the pause menu, and back out of a menu
bindings.notes: ESC IS NOT A NEUTRAL KEY HERE. It opens the pause menu and the game stops presenting. Found the hard way: an ESC sent as 'cleanup' after a probe silently froze rendering for several subsequent captures.
Both menus print their own controls on screen: 'ENTER SELECT, ESCAPE BACK'.
MUST carry KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY. Non-extended 0x50 and the 'S' key were both tested and did nothing at all.

states.name: gameplay
states.detect: Frame-to-frame screen difference is continuously non-zero (idle animation, grass, water). HUD present: health/shield bars top-left, ability radial bottom-left, item count bottom-right.

states.name: paused
states.detect: 'PAUSED' top-right; items RESUME GAME / OPTIONS / RESTART FROM LAST CHECKPOINT / EXIT TO MAIN MENU. Frame-to-frame difference is exactly 0.00 because the game stops presenting.
states.notes: The zero-difference signature is a reliable paused detector, but ONLY if frames are captured with BitBlt. See hazards: PrintWindow keeps serving a stale frame and will show gameplay while the game is actually paused.

states.name: main_menu
states.detect: Items CONTINUE JOURNEY / CHAPTER SELECT / NEW JOURNEY / EXTRAS / OPTIONS / CREDITS / QUIT over a character-portrait background.

states.name: loading
states.detect: Large sustained frame differences (100+) for tens of seconds after selecting CONTINUE JOURNEY. Reaching gameplay took roughly 20-40s.

states.name: cutscene
states.notes: ESC during a checkpoint cutscene did not obviously skip it; the pause menu appeared once the cutscene had ended.

steps: VERIFY 'EXIT TO MAIN MENU' is highlighted
Enter (confirms the warning that progress since the last checkpoint will be lost)
ensure CONTINUE JOURNEY is highlighted (it is the default on entry)
routes.notes: Lands at the last checkpoint, often inside a cutscene.
Process exits in about 4 seconds. This is the graceful close and should be preferred to terminating the process.
CHAPTER SELECT is present on the main menu but was NOT exercised. If it works it gives varied scenes on demand, which is valuable for reverse-engineering.

entry_points.notes: The window title contains trademark symbols and a line break. Match on the substring 'ENSLAVED' rather than the full string.

console.notes: DOES NOT OPEN BY KEYPRESS. Tilde (0x29, bound as ConsoleKey), Tab (0x0F, bound as TypeKey) and F10 (0x44) were each sent as scancodes to the focused window with a capture taken after; the scene was unchanged every time. Consistent with the console class being stripped from this shipping build, which is common in UE3 releases. This is n=3 keys, so it rules out the cheap route rather than every route. KEPT AS A DISPROVED ENTRY so the next reader does not repeat it.

keybinding_exec.notes: UE3 can bind a key directly to an exec command string, which is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the console - there is no prompt to type into. MonkeyInput.ini ships a DEVELOPER binding, Bindings=(Name="F9",Command="shot"), which is why this looks promising: 'shot' is an ordinary exec command bound to a key by the developers. Pressing F9 and looking for a screenshot file is the cheapest decisive test of the whole channel. Untested as of 2026-09-03 because input inis are read at load and the test needs a relaunch.

debug_camera.notes: MonkeyInput.ini ships a complete debug free-camera input map under [NTGameFramework.NTCam_DebugInput]: ToggleDebugCamera (Alt+C), WASD plus Q/E to fly including vertically, mouse look, LeftShift MoreSpeed, F FreezeRendering, End Pause, PageDown Step (frame stepping). If live, this is the engine's OWN free camera and solves most of 'move the camera to reverse-engineer the engine'. IMPORTANT: in normal gameplay its entry point is a CONTROLLER thumbstick chord (CheckDebugCamChord / DoDebugCamChord in [Engine.PlayerInput]), not a key - which is why pressing keys never finds it. Rebind it to a key in the ini instead. UNTESTED: a binding surviving in a shipped ini is NOT evidence the feature is live, because the console's bindings survive in this same file and the console is dead.

hazards.hazard: PrintWindow returns a STALE frame once the game stops presenting
hazards.notes: PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) is correct while the game renders, then keeps serving the last DWM-composited frame indefinitely, with no error, whenever the game pauses or sits in a menu. It is wrong exactly when the picture matters most. Tell: identical consecutive captures, and a delta that repeats at a constant value. Use BitBlt from the screen DC instead (it needs the window unoccluded); a proxy-side backbuffer readback beats both.

hazards.hazard: NEW JOURNEY sits two rows below CONTINUE JOURNEY on the main menu
hazards.notes: A miscounted Down keypress overwrites the save. Never blind key-count past a destructive item: navigate, capture, verify the highlight visually, and only then send Enter.

hazards.hazard: ESC is not a neutral key
hazards.notes: It opens the pause menu and stops rendering. Read the screen after any key you are not certain about, rather than assuming a keypress did nothing.

hazards.hazard: Config inis exist in TWO places, and the engine rewrites them on exit
hazards.notes: The live copy is under Documents\My Games\UnrealEngine3\MonkeyGame\Config\; the game folder holds a template plus Default*.ini. Editing only the game-folder copy does nothing. Set both, and edit them while the game is CLOSED, or the engine can overwrite the change on exit.

hazards.hazard: Whole-frame mean-luma difference is too blunt to score input routes in this game
hazards.notes: Animated grass, water and idle animation put a no-input control between 3.4 and 23.3, which is ABOVE the signal from a working keypress. That method scored a key which demonstrably walks the character as 'no effect'. Keep the no-input control - it is the right instinct - but prefer a large unmistakable action plus reading two screenshots. If a number is genuinely needed, camera motion is a coherent global translation (phase correlation), not a mean difference.
